    4.3 Follow-up Assessments:

All producers will be assessed annually, based on the same procedure and notice period.

    4.4 Random or unannounced assessments:

The Outeniqua PGS reserves the right to do random or unannounced visits to production premises
under the following circumstances:

                   . If a complaint IN WRITING is received regarding the product of any
                       farmer/producer, an unannounced visit may be scheduled. (see section on
                       dealing with non-compliance)

                   . A number of random visits can be undertaken to members prior to annual
                       assessments as part of quality management.

    4.5 Non-compliance and discipline:

PGS is at its most effective when all members are operating according to its rules and in the spirit
of organic principles. The first action to be taken in any case of ill-discipline or transgression is the
path of informal counselling, mentoring and practical assistance prior to any official action. It needs
to be understood that all members should conduct themselves according to the signed pledge and
comply with the Standard Operating Procedures and produce their goods in compliance with the
Basic Production Principles. If there is any reason to believe that any member is operating or
conducting him/herself outside the stated guidelines and the first action (if applicable), of inter-member guidance or counselling is ineffective, formal action may be instituted.

This will be done according to the following guidelines:
    1. Only complaints received in writing will be attended to. Our PGS cannot react to random
         or unfounded verbal complaints or allegations.
    2. Type of complaint:
                  a. If the complaint is regarding unacceptable production or farming practices, a
                       visit to the production premises will precede a complaint hearing. This visit
                       may be unannounced, and must include at least the administrator, a
                       committee member and one other unaffected member of our PGS. During this
                       visit, the same procedures will be followed as with a scheduled assessment,
                       with specific focus on the nature of the complaint. After the visit, the
                       procedures as described below will be followed.
                  b. If the complaint is regarding member conduct only, (a.) above will be deemed
                       unnecessary and procedure (c.) will be followed.
                  c. A minuted meeting will be called with the following persons present:
    1. The member against whom the complaint is levelled
    2. The administrator of the Outeniqua PGS
    3. A committee member of the Outeniqua PGS
              At least one additional group member or PGSSA member not involved in the
                  complaint.
              A person deemed competent to record the proceedings.

                                                                                                                6
          The complainant or authorised representative. If this is not possible, [the
              complainant will be expected to produce a written account of the complaint; in
              such case, the complainant shall accept the outcome of the ruling.

4. The complaint will be read to the member, and physical or documented proof and/or
    evidence will be presented. The member will have an opportunity to answer or explain
    his/her actions, and supply evidence or proof to substantiate his/her reply. If deemed
    necessary, the complainant may be present or be called for his/her response.

5. The meeting will rule on the validity of the complaint, after hearing both parties'
    submissions and may rule as follows:
         a. Rejection of complaint: If the complaint is deemed invalid, both parties will be
              informed and the decision recorded. The decision will be communicated in
              writing to affected parties.
         b. Acceptance of complaint: If the complaint is justified, action will be taken against
              the concerned member; the meeting will assess the level of misconduct,
              implement the appropriate action, and communicate the decision in writing to
              affected parties.

Action:    First warning: If this is the first time a member has transgressed a non-critical
           requirement, the member will receive a first warning. The warning will be active for
           one calendar year. Any action not described below in para. (c.) is deemed a non-critical transgression.
           Second warning: A second warning for a similar transgression during one calendar
           year will result in cancellation of membership.
           Serious misconduct: If the transgression is deemed to be serious misconduct,
           membership will be terminated immediately without a warning.

Examples of serious misconduct are:

 Public abuse (physical or otherwise) of fellow PGS members and/or customers.
 Any action that brings the PGS into disrepute.
 The use or application of any substance or additive specifically prohibited by the

    SAOSO Standard for Organic Production and Processing or by the Basic Production
    Principles. For example, any production practices that could impact on the organic
    nature of the end product, i.e. the addition of unacceptable inputs, intentional use of
    GMOs, contamination of the product with pollutants, chemicals etc.
 The failure to implement corrective actions marked as critical as required during a
    PGS assessment visit.
 Any criminal action as described in the Statutes and Laws of the Republic of South
    Africa.
 The sale of any un-assessed product bearing our PGS endorsement logo or otherwise
    marketed as a PGS endorsed product.
 The sale of any product bearing the logo or registration number of a third-party
    certifier, or otherwise marketed as organic, and found not to be compliant with the
    requirements of the certifying body. Such a transgression will also be reported to the
    relevant certifier.

Termination of membership will be seen as a last resort. The committee is required to take into
account mitigating circumstances.
